text: Every program you run needs somewhere to keep its stuff. That place is called the heap. Picture it as a warehouse.
Each time your code creates something, like a user, a cart, or a photo, a box lands in the warehouse. Your code holds on to each box with a cable.
When your code lets go, the cable disappears. A cleaning robot, the garbage collector, sees that nothing is attached, and hauls the box away.
A leak is a box you're done with that's still tied to something. Here, a cache keeps a cable on every old page. The robot isn't allowed to touch them.
So the old pages pile up, until the warehouse is full. Your app slows down, and eventually it crashes.
A heap snapshot is a photo of the whole warehouse. Every box, how big it is, and what's holding on to it.
Take one photo, repeat the action, and take another. Whatever grew is your leak. Follow its cables back, and you'll find the code that's holding it.
